speaker: champion:emergent
text: I didn’t plan it, {title}. I did it once, and now it’s everywhere: {emergent}. Newcomers think you invented it. Could it be official? Properly official?

choices.label: Make it official.
choices.reaction: {emergentBy} reads the announcement aloud twice. By the next {meeting}, {emergent} has a laminated explanation.

choices.label: Let it carry on as it is.
choices.hint: Tolerate · It grows on its own
choices.reaction: {emergentBy} is a little disappointed and entirely unstopped. It carries on, unofficially and with growing confidence.

speaker: agenda:purity
text: Point of order. Nobody voted on {emergent}. It was started by {emergentBy}, it appears in no minutes, and most of the membership now does it. Either it is ours or it is not.

choices.label: It isn’t ours. Stop it.
choices.reaction: The ruling is read at the {meeting}. Nobody argues. Several people do it anyway on the way out.

choices.label: It’s ours now. Leave it.
choices.reaction: {speaker} writes “tolerated” in the minutes and underlines it in a way that suggests a footnote is coming.

speaker: agenda:order
text: {emergent} has no procedure. People do it differently in every room. I’d like to write it down properly: when, how, and who decides. Otherwise it’s just… happening.

choices.label: Write the rules for it.
choices.reaction: {speaker} produces a four-page procedure. {emergentBy} reads it and says it is the same thing, but worse. Members adopt the procedure and quietly keep the original.

choices.label: Some things should just happen.
choices.reaction: {speaker} says “just happen” the way other people say “mould”. It carries on happening.

text: Can I ask something? There’s a new thing going round: {emergent}. We’ve all been at it for weeks. Is that allowed? Nobody said it was. Nobody said it wasn’t. I’d like to know before I teach it to my mother.

choices.label: It’s allowed. It’s encouraged.
choices.reaction: The mother in question learns it by the weekend and teaches it to her bridge club. {emergent} is now, officially, ours.

choices.label: Please don’t teach it to your mother.
choices.reaction: Nobody tells the mother. She finds out anyway and is, by all accounts, furious about being excluded from something.

speaker: any
text: {emergent} has grown. There are workshops now. A newcomer asked me which came first, {belief} or {emergent}. I didn’t know what to say, {title}. Do you?

choices.label: Take it on officially.
choices.reaction: You announce that {emergent} has, in a sense, always been part of {movement}. {emergentBy} is delighted to hear it.

choices.label: It’s gone too far. End it.
choices.reaction: The ban is announced. A smaller, more committed group carries on in the car park, with a lookout.

speaker: any
text: Since you made {emergent} official, members have developed an advanced version. It takes longer and involves more people, and there is now a beginners’ version that nobody wants to be seen doing.

choices.label: Let it evolve.
choices.reaction: There are now three versions. Newcomers are given a leaflet. The leaflet has an advanced version.

choices.label: One version. The one I approved.
choices.reaction: The advanced version is retired. Its practitioners describe themselves as “between versions”.

speaker: any
text: It’s still going on: {emergent}. Quietly, after the {meeting}, in the car park. They have a lookout. The lookout is asleep, but the principle stands.

choices.label: Fine. Bring it back inside.
choices.reaction: {emergent} returns indoors to a standing ovation, which members insist was spontaneous.

choices.label: A ban is a ban.
choices.reaction: The car park is patrolled. The practice moves to a different car park. There are a lot of car parks.

speaker: any
text: The people who started {emergent} say your reformed version has lost its soul. They’ve started doing the original again, slightly louder, as a protest.

choices.label: Restore the original.
choices.reaction: The original returns. It is, everyone agrees, exactly as good as before, plus a small amount of triumph.

choices.label: The reformed version stays.
choices.reaction: The originalists form a small society. It meets at the same time as everyone else, in the same room, facing the other way.

text: Quick question for the profile. Readers love {emergent}. It’s the bit everyone mentions. Was it your idea?

choices.label: It was {emergentBy}’s idea.
choices.reaction: The profile runs with a photograph of {emergentBy}, who buys forty copies.

choices.label: Everything here started with me.
choices.reaction: The profile calls you the visionary behind {emergent}. {emergentBy} cuts it out, frames it and hangs it upside down.
